summary: A companion to Around and Under that routes study by passing direction and distinguishes retention from later offense.
description: Locate an around-the-legs, north-south or under-the-legs retention problem in the Giles–Tabak anthology outline.
overview: This release organizes retention by the passer’s route and then adds specific situations. Identify the route first; a familiar pass name alone may hide where the exchange became difficult.

guide.display_title: Giles and Tabak: Guard Retention Around and Under

fits: Your recurring guard loss involves a passer moving around the legs, toward north-south, or underneath the legs.
consider_alternative_if: If you can retain guard and now need posture-specific K-guard entries and offense, compare Lachlan Giles’s K-Guard guide.

includes: General concepts and movements, followed by around-the-legs, north-south and under-the-legs retention.
Specific passing situations, stack-related material and rolling breakdowns.
limits: Through-the-legs and close-range study belongs to a separate companion release described by the publisher; this course is the Around and Under selection.

start_here.title: Name the route before the pass
start_here.task: Use one guard-loss exchange from your notes or footage. Record whether the passer went around your legs, reached north-south, or went underneath them. Match that description to parts 3, 4 or 5, and compare it with the opening general-concepts section before choosing a specific-pass lesson.
